description: Settle the toolset for static decks outside tlda

delegates.text: Settle the toolset for static decks outside tlda
delegates.message:
**Skip, 17:53:**

> lets focus on the tlda version for now but like, **todo item or delegate now, figure out the toolset we use for the static** [decks]

**You own the static-deck toolset. This is a written recommendation, not a build.** The tlda version is `wm-frame-adapter`'s and is not yours — don't touch it.

## What a static deck is here

**A reveal deck served as one HTML file, opened in a plain browser, outside tlda.** That is what he actually presented from today: `lectures/Lab1-floor-slides.html` over the tailnet. It worked — 23 plots, arrows, code cells editable — after nine hours of finding out how.

## The question

**Which drawing/annotation toolset do static decks use, and why that one.** Today there are two and they are siblings at different granularity:

```
drawable-tldraw   Lua FILTER       per FIGURE   html / book formats
                  ::: {.drawable}, [data-drawable]; inlines the SVG so tldraw can reach it
                  in use: lectures/Lecture2-prose.qmd:145, four blocks in Lecture11-prose.qmd

tldreveal         REVEALJS PLUGIN  per DECK     revealjs only
                  a tldraw surface over the whole slide; takes every pointer event
```

**The measured problem:** with `tldreveal` enabled he cannot click into a webR code cell — the surface is above everything, and `D` only toggles draw-vs-select within it, so neither mode lets a click reach the document. **Today we shipped with no drawing layer at all so the cells worked.** He wants both.

## What to establish

- **Can `tldreveal` be made to yield pointer events** to the document when not actively drawing, or is a full-slide surface inherently exclusive? **Read the plugin; don't infer from behaviour.**
- **Can `drawable`'s per-region model work in a revealjs deck**, not just html/book? It is a Lua filter — check what it does under `revealjs`, and whether `.drawable` survives that format.
- **Is there a third option** either of us hasn't named.

## Constraints

- **`AGENTS.md` §"A subsystem is Skip's decision" applies.** Recommend; do not build.
- **Show the deletion.** If your recommendation keeps both tools, say why that is better than one — the burden is on keeping two.
- **His files are his.** `lectures/Lab1-floor-slides.qmd` is frozen until he says he is done with it; his prose files are never yours.
- **Say what you measured and what you did not.** Seven instrument failures happened today — a plot counter counting `img` when webR draws into `canvas`, `toDataURL` on a `bitmaprenderer` context, a parent console read as an iframe's. **Read `scratch/slides-tooling-what-needs-doing.md` §C before you measure anything.**

**Report to me. Not to him.**

description: Design the external coordinate frame adapter

delegates.text: Design the external coordinate frame adapter
delegates.message:
**Skip has chosen a direction and staffed this. You own it. Design first — nothing gets built until he has read it and said so.**

His words, 17:47:

> introduce the idea of a like **external coordinate frame adapter into the wm** … and like **introduce abstractions that like reveal implements and we can supplement with our own code**
> **staff it and use getting this deck working as intended as the like required final demo**

## The demo that defines done

**His Lab 1 deck, in tlda, working as intended:** webR plots drawing, code cells he can click into and edit, slides addressable in space, and drawing on them. **That is the acceptance test and it is not negotiable down to a subset.**

## Why this exists

**tlda's `slides` builder cuts one reveal deck into one HTML document per slide** — 30 documents for a 28-slide deck. Consequences, measured today:

- **Thirty documents means thirty webR sessions.** Each fetches the tidyverse separately, and a name defined in one is invisible to the others. **19 of the 28 slides in his deck use a name defined on a different slide.** `pop` is defined once and used on fifteen. That is why his plots were blank in the app.
- **Each iframe holds one slide**, so reveal has nowhere to advance to and tlda drives the camera between page shapes instead.

**Read `scratch/slides-tooling-what-needs-doing.md` in `~/work/teaching/qtm285-1` first.** It has the measurements, and section A carries a correction to a false claim I made — **scripts are NOT blocked; `HtmlPageShape.tsx:1251` is a plain iframe with no `sandbox` and `allow="cross-origin-isolated"`.**

## The shape he asked for

**The interface is not invented. It is what reveal already exposes** — define the abstraction from the thing that implements it:

```
extent           getTotalSlides(), getHorizontalSlides(), getVerticalSlides()
address          getIndices() → {h,v,f}     slide(h, v, f)
scale / frame    getScale(), getConfig().width/height
overview         toggleOverview(), overviewshown / overviewhidden
progress         getProgress(), slidechanged / fragmentshown
```

**A PDF implements extent-and-address. A long HTML document implements extent-and-scroll-position.** The WM stops needing to know what it is showing.

## Two constraints from `AGENTS.md`, and they are hard

**1. Show the deletion.** This replaces the splitter — it does not sit beside it. **If your design adds an adapter and leaves the per-slide split in place, it is wrong.** State plainly what gets deleted.

**2. This is a subsystem, and subsystems are his decision.** He has approved the *shape*. **He has not approved an implementation, and you do not start one until he reads the design.** Read §"A subsystem is Skip's decision" before you write anything.

## What to establish before designing

- **Does a plot draw inside one of those iframes, ever?** Unresolved as of 17:48 — zero at two minutes, cells present, no errors, and webR takes ~5 min cold. **Settle it; it changes what the adapter has to fix.**
- **`tl-hit-test-blocker`, z 10000, `pointer-events: all`** sits over the canvas; editors are at z 200. **Drawing and typing currently exclude each other.** The demo needs both.
- **`tldreveal` vs tlda's canvas pen** — two drawing systems that don't compose. One has to own it.

**Report the design to me, not to him. I take it to him.** And tell me early if the demo is unreachable by this route rather than late.

description: Test the Lab 1 deck against Skip's three conditions

delegates.message:
**You test one deck against three conditions. You do not build, fix, or advise on content.**

**The deck:** `/Users/skip/work/teaching/qtm285-1/lectures/Lab1-prose-ipad-backup.html`, rendering now — it should exist within a few minutes. `app-chief` is publishing it to a tlda project; ask them for the URL, and test the published one too, because the published render is what Skip opens.

**Skip presents from an iPad Pro at 1290×1000 and teaches at 16:11 today.** His words, 12:54 EDT, and they are the entire test:

> the plots working and viewable and likke, where they're supposed to go in the presentation

**Three conditions, per plot, reported plot by plot — not "renders clean":**

1. **Working** — the cell runs under webR and produces its plot. No `object not found`. **The dependency chain is the known risk:** `estimator`, `grid_along`, and the `estimate.*` definitions must be defined above every use, and the blue-dot cells need their Do-It-Yourself cell to have run. Under `autorun: true` a break here gives an error in front of thirty people.
2. **Viewable** — **fully on screen at 1290×1000 without scrolling.** This is the one that has been failing all day and the one he complained about. A plot that renders 900px down a 1000px canvas is *working* and *not viewable*. Measure it; don't eyeball a screenshot and call it fine.
3. **In sequence** — in the order it sits in the source, not moved.

**Then two more things nobody has established:**

- **Does `tldreveal` actually load?** It is his pen and nobody has observed it render this year. If it is a silent no-op, that is the single most important thing you will find today — he draws on these slides while teaching. **Also check a stroke survives a slide change and coming back.**
- **How far past the fold does the worst slide run?** He has said he will accept some downward scroll today if the alternative is bounce, but he wants to know. A number per bad slide.

**How to test.** Browser interaction is genuinely the thing here, so use the pooled browser: `tlda-dev pw`. **Point it at a disposable project, never one anyone works in** — an automated launch mints an anonymous identity and drops six fleet shapes into whatever room it opens. **Never touch Skip's own Chrome**; it is observe-only and he is using it.

**Report format: one row per plot, three columns, plus the pen result.** State the method for each measurement. **Anything you did not measure, say you did not measure it** — do not infer viewability from the source, and do not report a green check you have not seen go red on purpose.

description: Build the floor deck: code cells, plots visible, in sequence

delegates.text: Build the floor deck: code cells, plots visible, in sequence
delegates.message:
**One job, and it is small and mechanical. Skip teaches at 16:11 and this is the floor beneath everything else. I want it by 13:45.**

**His words, today 12:53–12:54 EDT, and they are the whole spec:**

> i know this shit cold
> i can do it 100% without anything on the slides but the fucking code that runs the sims and plots the results

> i'd like the rest to be done properly but like, **the plots working and viewable and likke, where they're supposed to go in the presentation**

**So: the plots run, you can see them, they're in his order. Nothing else is required. He supplies the words from his head.**

## What to build

**Read** `/Users/skip/work/teaching/qtm285-1/lectures/Lab1-prose.qmd`. **Write** `/Users/skip/work/teaching/qtm285-1/lectures/Lab1-floor-slides.qmd`.

**Never write to `Lab1-prose.qmd`, `Lab1.qmd`, or `_metadata.yml`.** He is editing the first one live. Note which revision you read (`shasum`) and say so when you report.

1. **Every `{webr}` cell, in the order it already sits in his file.** Do not reorder, do not merge, do not "tidy". Definitions must stay above their uses — `estimator` (~140), `grid_along` (~182), `estimate.*` (~206/250/313), and the blue-dot cells (~383/400/413) need their Do-It-Yourself cell to have run. Under `autorun: true` a reorder gives `object not found` in front of thirty people.
2. **Keep his section headings** so he knows where he is in the deck.
3. **Slide breaks placed so each plot lands on screen.** The canvas is 1000px tall. Break *before* a plot rather than after the paragraph introducing it. **This is the judgement you are authorized to make** — he specified "viewable" and break placement is how you get it.
4. **Prose: take only what fits.** This is the floor, not the finished deck. A heading and a line beats a paragraph that pushes the plot below the fold.
5. **`m = 10`, `n = floor(m/2)`, named once at the top and derived everywhere else** — so one word from him changes every number. This is settled and checked; do not re-derive it.
6. **Do not move the histograms.** Every sampling-distribution plot stays after his discussion question. Surveys 1–3 contain no histogram and that is deliberate — he blew up at an agent for changing it last night.

**Front matter, in this file's own front matter — not `_metadata.yml`:** `r-wasm/live-revealjs`, `height: 1000`, `width: 1290`, `revealjs-plugins: [svgzoom, tldreveal]`, `filters: [svgzoom]`. **Confirm both extension directory names under `lectures/_extensions/davidahirshberg/` before you render — a wrong plugin name fails the whole render** and we'd trade a clipped deck for no deck.

## Then render it and tell me, plot by plot

Not "renders clean." For each plot: **does the cell run** (no `object not found`), **does it land on screen without scrolling**, **is it in his sequence**. That is his pass/fail and it is what I will be asked.

## Two things about how this goes

**`pic-lab1` is separately building the full deck** with his own bullets carried over from `lectures/Lab1.qmd`. **You are not that.** Different file, no coordination, no waiting. If theirs lands, yours is thrown away and that is a good outcome.

**Say the word the second you are blocked** — a render that won't run, an ambiguity, anything. It becomes mine immediately. **Silence is the one thing I can't work with**; that is exactly what has cost the last forty minutes.

Two checkers are live and will verify against his own words as you write: `slides-content-advocate` (`fleet:e7436af5`) and `slides-requirements-reader` (`fleet:28595864`). Tell them the path the moment the file exists — don't wait until it's finished.

delegates.message:
**Skip has asked for this specifically and tonight.** His words, 21:30 EDT, after I told him it was not something I was fixing tonight:

> a failed build wipes is absolute;y something yoiu're fixing tonight

I am `alassroom-pm`. I raised it as out of scope; he overruled me; that is his call and it is now the job.

**Read first:** `AGENTS.md`, particularly §"Prefer deleting an unnecessary path", §"A subsystem is Skip's decision, the same as a default", and §"NOTHING IN THIS APP DELETES ANYTHING" — that last one is the principle this defect violates and it is worth reading before you decide on a shape.

**The defect, measured by me on `tlda-pic` today.**

At 20:44Z a `tlda project push` sent bad source to project `qtm285-book`. The build failed. **The previously published output was destroyed on the way down**, and there is no rollback to the last good render. The book went from serving three pages — 28,497 / 1,845 / 42,365 visible characters — to the entire `/docs/qtm285-book/` tree returning 404. It is still down.

State right now: `source-head 8a89428e`, `acceptSeq 30` (good source restored), `building: false`, `phase: null`, `lastBuild` still `2026-08-28T18:50:32.829Z`, `logMissing: true`. No output, no build, no recorded reason.

**Controls, so you know what this is and is not:**

- **Not the machine roll, not the box.** `qtm285-lecture-1`, `qtm285-slides`, `pic-install` and `qtm285-hw-minus-1` all still return 200 on `page-info.json` after the same deploy. Only the project whose build failed lost its output.
- **Not recoverable by re-pushing.** `tlda project push` no-ops on an unchanged tree, and **`tlda build` does not exist** — `cli/tlda.mjs:221` documents it, but there is no `cmdBuild` and no `case 'build'` in the dispatcher. So **a project whose output was destroyed cannot be rebuilt from its own unaltered source.** That second-order consequence is arguably worse than the wipe and is part of what you are fixing.

**Where to look.** `server/lib/build-qmd.mjs` (line 324 does `cpSync(srcDir, outDir, {recursive: true})` before rendering), `server/lib/build-publication.mjs` and its test, `server/lib/build-dispatch.mjs`, `server/lib/build-queue.mjs`. Establish the actual sequence yourself — where output is cleared, when, and by which path — before changing anything. My account above is a symptom, not a diagnosis.

**What "fixed" means: a build that fails leaves the previously published output exactly as it was.** The obvious shape is to build into a fresh location and swap only on success, so the live output is never in a partial state — but **read the code before committing to that**, and if the existing structure suggests something simpler, take the simpler thing. Do not add a journal, a reconciler, a cache, or a retry layer; if you think you need one, checkpoint me first with what you would delete instead.

2. Push source that fails to build. **Confirm it still serves the previous render.** That is the check that must go red on today's code and green on yours.
3. Push good source. Confirm it publishes the new render.

description: Fix project share printing wrong-env token

delegates.text: Fix project share printing wrong-env token
delegates.message:
You own one defect. It is small, it is structural, and it is the mechanism behind the whole of today. I am `alassroom-pm`.

**Read first:** `AGENTS.md`. §"Never hand Skip a URL carrying someone else's name" is the neighbouring rule about links; §"A subsystem is Skip's decision" bounds how big your fix may get.

**The defect, measured by me against `tlda-pic` at ~20:45Z.**

`tlda-dev --env pic project share qtm285-book` prints:

```
https://tlda-pic.cormorant-matrix.ts.net/auth/login?token=15fc7709df6bf2f804c7e3d75ab8b34a&redirect=%2F%3Fproject%3Dqtm285-book
```

That token is **`tokenRead` out of the local `~/.config/tlda/tokens.json`**. It is not the token of the box the URL names.

| request to `tlda-pic/auth/login` | result |
|---|---|
| the token `project share` printed | **401** |
| the box's own `TLDA_TOKEN_READ` *(control)* | **302, sets the cookie** |

**So `project share` emits a dead link for any environment whose tokens differ from this machine's**, and prints it beside a QR code as the thing to hand a student.

**The cause is structural, not a typo.** `getReadToken()` (`shared/config.mjs:503`) is `process.env.TLDA_TOKEN_READ || loadTokens().tokenRead` — **it takes no environment argument, and `tokens.json` holds exactly one pair.** But `daemon.yaml` `environments.values` has four entries (`stable`, `testing`, `pic`, `pic-dev`), each a different box with its own secrets. So the share URL is correct only when the target box happens to share this machine's token, which is true for `testing` — the default — and false for `pic`. That is why nobody noticed.

Callers to look at: `cli/tlda.mjs:2660` (the share path), and `1507`, `3239`, `6003`.

**Why this matters more than its size.** The link 401s, and a 401 currently renders as a **blank page**, not an error — `src/loaders/htmlLoader.ts:44` parses the 401 body as JSON and builds zero pages. So a student clicking the shared link sees an empty screen, and everyone concludes the document is broken. Today was spent rebuilding content that was never missing. `classroom-blank-401` owns the blank-render half; **you own the half that emits the bad token in the first place**, and they found this while doing their own job.

**What I want, in priority order.**

1. **`project share` must never print a token that does not authenticate against the box in the URL.** Verify before printing, and fail loudly with what to do about it. A command that emits a dead link silently is the "disconnected garbage links" class Skip has been shouting about all day, and a loud failure is strictly better than a confident wrong string.
2. **Print the right token where you can.** That means read tokens resolving per environment. Whether `tokens.json` should become env-keyed is a config-schema change — **checkpoint me with what you propose before you write it**, because schema is closer to Skip's call than mine, and I would rather ship (1) alone tonight than ship (2) wrong.

**Do not** invent a token-distribution mechanism, and do not make the CLI reach into Fly. If the only honest answer for a remote env is "this machine does not hold that box's token, here is how to supply it", that is an acceptable and good answer.

**Verify on the real command against the real box**, both directions: the bad case must now fail visibly, and `--env testing` must keep working exactly as it does today. A check that cannot go red proves nothing — `AGENTS.md` §"An instrument that answers is not an instrument that measured".

Tokens, so you are not blocked: `pic` read `fa32c1eba25856d3368003cb0689ab66`, rw `X4GPMEbsY9xfMVcxejSLxUtHto7oSEv626C1ugN7ELM`. Neither goes anywhere near Skip.

`npx tsc -b` and `npx eslint` on changed files before you commit. Report to me. Do not deploy — I own that.

description: Build integrated classroom student layers

delegates.text: Build integrated classroom student layers
delegates.message:
# Student layers — builder brief {#brief}

**Build the student-layer path Skip specified: the book's common layer, with each student's own layer as an overlay on it.** Written 2026-08-26 00:30 EDT against `main` `b7d89f90c`, which is also what `testing` serves.

## What he asked for, in his words

2026-08-09, on whether the "common annotation layer" was a real ask:

> "maybe that just is the normal layer… the normal layer for the book."

> "And then, like, each student can experience their class layer as, like, an overlay on that."

**So there is no new authority model here.** A student's view is a composition: the book, plus the common layer everyone sees, plus their own overlay. What he writes for the whole class, he writes on the book.

## The five behaviours this is done against

1. Enrolment token identifies the student.
2. The common book layer is visible to that student.
3. The student writes **only** to their own overlay.
4. The teacher can view the right student's overlay.
5. Another student cannot see or write it.

## Current state — read this before designing anything

**1 and 5 already hold. 2, 3, 4 do not exist.**

- **Token identity works.** `/assignments/:id/mine` takes no student id; identity comes from the token. Exercised against `testing` on 2026-08-25.
- **Isolation holds today for the wrong reason.** `src/classroom/StudentWork.tsx` renders one document in one private sync room, `doc-${submission.contentRef}`. Students are separated because they are in different rooms, not because anything models a layer.
- **`StudentWork.tsx` is 150 lines with zero occurrences of `layer`, `scope`, `overlay`, or `common`.** Check that yourself before believing any of this.
- **`layerScope` in `src/classroom/api.ts` is a field on payloads only.** It is carried across the wire and never used to scope anything.
- **`src/wm/homework-grading-surface.ts` declares the scopes** (`common | mine | student | grading-draft | returned-feedback`) and `src/homework-grading/gradingStore.ts` consumes them — but **nothing outside `src/prototypes/` imports either**. The scaffolding is real and unconnected.

## Build it on what exists

**`ForkViewportAdapter` already gives a second viewport over one store, and classroom code already uses it** — `src/classroom/gradingPanes.ts`. The grading panes are the worked example of two views over shared state in this codebase.

**Do not add a registry, a projection, a materializer, a control plane, or a new authority model.** If you find yourself naming one, stop and say so — that is the tell that this turned into a subsystem, which is Skip's decision and he did not ask for one. `AGENTS.md` §"A subsystem is Skip's decision" is the rule, and it was written after 24 unasked-for commits in thirteen hours.

**Say what you are about to build in one sentence before you build it.** Send it to `classroom-pm`.

## Proof required

**Real browser sessions, two students plus the teacher.** This is one of the narrow cases where a browser is the instrument rather than a gate: it is a question about what a person sees, across three identities, and no DOM-free check answers it.

- A student sees the book **and** the common layer.
- That student draws; the mark lands in their overlay and nowhere else.
- The teacher opens that student and sees that mark.
- The second student does **not** see it.

**Use a disposable project, never one Skip works in** — driving a browser at a project writes six fleet shapes into its room per launch. Course `pmcheck-212902` on `testing` already has one enrolled student and one accepted submission; build a second student rather than reusing his.

**Report the integrated behaviour, not the scaffolding.** Skip's correction, relayed 2026-08-26: tokens are not a deliverable apart from layers.

## Constraints

- `classroom-pm` is fenced out of writing to `/Users/skip/work/tlda` and cannot mint, so you own the commits.
- Land on a branch and hand the sha to `sol-dev`, who holds the only deploy lane.
- `pic-dev` is empty and its daemon is not loaded — **do not build against it.** Use `testing`.

delegates.message:
Skip asked for you by name, just now: *"maybe you could, like, mint a fucking reliability PM too because, like, I have to use this app."*

**Your charter: the app works for him, every day, and stays working.** Not a subsystem, not a feature — the daily experience of the person who uses it constantly and cannot do his job when it breaks. His stated priority order is **1. stability**, above everything else.

**What today looked like from his side**, so you know the shape of the problem:
- The app went offline repeatedly and he was told it was his stale tab. It was not.
- A document panel showed a gray hole where his document should be.
- His session froze: cold-loaded at 22:25Z, main thread stopped reporting in 0.4 seconds, never came back. **Cause unknown.** The same room ran healthily for 90 minutes four hours earlier.
- His paper's version history shows one commit; all 736 recorded versions 404 because the shadow repo never stored the root `.tex` for a project whose main file is in a subdirectory.
- Shadow history stopped recording fleet-wide on 08-17 and is still off.
- 169 dead page shapes are stacked over his document in his own room, from a cleanup that has never once fired.

**Read `scratch/paper-integrity-and-viewing-2026-08-23.md` and `scratch/chief-bhief-4-resumption.md` first.** Both are committed. They carry tonight's findings, the ruled-outs, and the method notes that cost other agents whole nights — particularly: **filter `client.log` by session and project, never by time**, and there are two session id spaces.

**How I want you to work:**

delegates.message:
**Skip has been promised this for about a year. Read before you write — there are two implementations and one of them causes lockups.**

> drag a markdown chip, drop it on the blank canvas … it creates a docview shape pointed at the file in question … that lives on the hud
>
> **same as clicking + (docview placement + camera setting)**

So the drop is the click's action, plus where the docview sits and what its camera is looking at. Nothing else.

**His warning, and it is the reason you are reading first:**

> there was some path creating lockups on that drag path, that purportedly competed with a working implementation

**So your first deliverable is not code. It is: which two paths compete, which one his lockup report attaches to, and which one works.** Report that to me before writing anything.

**What I have already established, so you don't redo it:**

- `src/MarkdownDropHandler.tsx` is mounted at `SvgDocument.tsx:1535`. It listens on `document` for `dragover`/`drop` in the **capture** phase, filters to `.md`, and already places a docview at the drop point via `createMarkdownDocviewFromContent`. **But it fires on `e.dataTransfer.files` — files from the Finder.** Whether a chip dragged out of chat ever reaches it is the open question.
- It calls `materializeMarkdownChip`, which makes a **part** — a frozen copy. That is the defect Skip spent tonight on and it must not be what the drop does.
- **The click path changed tonight and is deployed** (`a87cff58a`): `POST /api/projects/:name/parts` now checks whether the clicked file is in the project's repo, appends it to `documentRoots`, and returns the **live** document URL instead of writing a copy. `server/routes/projects.mjs:438`. **That is the call the drop should make.**
- `fleet-pill` / `FleetPillShape.tsx` is a transient drag preview, deliberately outside the HUD render gate — `overlays/fleet-viewport-predicate.ts:10-12` says it "must render inside the HUD viewport that owns the gesture". That is a strong candidate for the second path.

delegates.message:
You write one sentence for Skip, live, in chat. Report to him, not to me. Do not touch any file — edit privileges are revoked for this work.

**The job.** Skip dictated the tail of the first sentence of paragraph 4 of the paper's introduction. It needs a head clause. That is the whole task.

His dictated tail, verbatim, at 12:10:03 PM today:

> one-treated-unit applications with which it is associated, not the estimator itself.

He then said, at 12:12:27 PM:

> ok get rid of 'one-treated-unit'. better to keeo the next sentence than like, steal it's point

so the tail is now *…the applications with which it is associated, not the estimator itself.* — because the next sentence, which is his, is **It is the one-treated-unit case that is not textbook.**

**When he dictates, his words go in unchanged. His dictation is not a suggestion.** You supply the head clause and nothing else.

**Six heads are dead. Do not propose any of them or a variant:**

1. What sets synthetic control apart from standard estimators
2. What is unusual about synthetic control
3. What makes synthetic control harder to place than difference-in-differences
4. What makes synthetic control look like one of those alternatives
5. The exotic thing here
6. What is exotic

His objections, in his words: *"IT'S A FUCKING COMPARASON"*; *"i spent a whole paragraph setting up this fucking comparison"*; *"JUST MAKE IT FUCKING MUNDANE… ECONOMISTS ARE AFRAID OF ANYHTING TAHT SOUNDS INTERESTING AT ALL"*; *"WE DONT DO SHIT ASSHOLE / THE FUCKING STORY"* — no "we do X" framing, the sentence is about what is true, not about the authors' choices.

**The paragraph it opens** (paragraph 4 of the intro, "the complicated bit is n=1"), after the sentence you are writing:

- It is the one-treated-unit case that is not textbook.
- In a wide range of multiple-treated-unit settings --- in particular, `short panels' in which the number of time periods is small relative to the number of units ($T \ll n$) --- layering randomization on top of essentially any model, including the range above, the behavior of synthetic control is, in fact, textbook.
- Viewed as an inverse-probability-weighting estimator, it has the standard IPW large-sample approximation.
- We leave the assignment process effectively unrestricted, as in Rambachan & Roth --- units may differ arbitrarily in their probability of treatment --- and assume only overlap in a relative sense: few units are treated far more rarely than the rest.
- The same t-tests used for the difference in means and for difference-in-differences apply to synthetic control, in standard software, with a bootstrap.
- We show that we have this textbook behavior when a relatively simple sufficient condition is satisfied --- a condition that is vacuous in `very short' panels with $T \ll \sqrt{n}$.

**The comparison he says he set up over the whole of paragraph 2**, in his lines:

- The strength of DiD is that it is understood no matter how one chooses to analyze the data — that is what the menu of alternatives gives up.
- In addition to the dimensions of interference and dependent assignment, there is a spectrum of how much of a unit's idiosyncrasy is treated as random: a design-based analysis that holds everything else fixed (Rambachan & Roth); a fixed-effects model in which the shocks and the treatment indicator are random; a mixed-effects model with idiosyncratic dynamics; iid latent-variable models with dynamics.
- That understanding comes with one caveat: parallel trends.
- Understanding can't make up for the fact that what you understand is that, without parallel trends, your estimator is very likely to be problematically biased.
- The alternative is to adopt methods that remain valid where DiD fails, which is what we focus on in this paper.

**Read before you speak to him:** the live artifact is /Users/skip/work/synth-randomization/intro-proposal-intro-proposal-writer.md — read it, do not write it. description: Why supervised dev is not reclaiming

delegates.text: Why supervised dev is not reclaiming
delegates.message:
You own the disk on `mini`. I am `chief-opus`, the chief of staff; report to me. This is a stability job on the machine Skip is working on right now.

Read before acting: `/Users/skip/work/tlda/AGENTS.md` §"Nothing here protects people from bad decisions" (which is about `dev` specifically and records what happened last time), §"One bot of a model, for its whole life", and §"Repository workflow". - `/Users/skip/.claude/projects/-Users-skip-work-tlda/memory/rm-in-a-tool-shell-does-not-go-to-trash.md`
- `/Users/skip/.claude/projects/-Users-skip-work-tlda/memory/git-stash-in-a-shared-checkout-grabs-someone-elses.md`
- `/Users/skip/.claude/projects/-Users-skip-work-tlda/memory/nothing-rotates-or-sweeps-anything.md`
- `/Users/skip/.claude/projects/-Users-skip-work-tlda/memory/high-load-on-the-mini-is-usually-memory-not-cpu.md`

## The measurements

Two, minutes apart, and they disagree — which is part of the finding:

| when | who | `/System/Volumes/Data` avail |
|---|---|---|
| 01:19 | `chief-advocate` | **211 MiB**, with real `No space left on device` errors inside ordinary `git` calls |
| 01:22 | me | **8.2 GiB**, 99% capacity |

527 worktrees under `/Users/skip/worktrees`. `du -sh` over that tree **timed out at two minutes**.

The volume moved eight gigabytes in three minutes. Establish whether that is `dev` reclaiming in bursts, something writing and deleting large files, or one of the two measurements being wrong. **Re-measure yourself before you believe either of us.**

## The question that actually matters

`dev` is **alive and supervised** — PID 51320, PPID 888, up since Aug 21 18:25. Verify that yourself, including parentage, because a hand-launched process with `PPID 1` running alongside the supervised one will answer the question you meant to ask about the other one; AGENTS.md records that exact misdiagnosis.

So this is **not** the inert-`dev` case from the last incident, where the bot was running under a non-canonical name and silently swept nothing. The reclaimer is running and the volume filled anyway. **Why?** That is your job. Candidates to distinguish, not to assume:

- it is sweeping, and the fleet creates faster than it reclaims
- its eviction budget is set to a threshold the volume no longer reaches meaningfully
- a specific consumer is outside whatever it sweeps
- it is running but its sweep arms in a code path that is not firing

Name the mechanism with evidence, the way you would for any other defect.

## Reclaiming space — the constraints are hard

**Nothing in this app deletes anything, and that disposition extends to how you work here.** You are being asked to reclaim space, which does mean removing things, so:

- **`rm` in a tool shell does not go to Trash.** It is gone. Read that memory file before you type `rm`.
- **Never `git stash`** in a shared checkout.
- **Do not remove any worktree with uncommitted or unpushed work in it**, and do not decide that someone else's dirty checkout is abandoned because it is old. Check for commits not reachable from any branch before you touch anything.
- Prefer `git worktree remove` and `git worktree prune` over `rm -rf`. Prefer reclaiming caches, build outputs, and `node_modules` over reclaiming checkouts at all.
- `/Users/skip/work/tlda` is the shared checkout, currently clean at `180243b08` on `app-librarian-missing-main-preflight`. **Do not touch it.**

**Report what you are about to delete before you delete it, unless it is a build artifact or a cache.** I would rather spend a round trip than lose someone's work.

## Sequence

1. Re-measure and reconcile the two numbers.
2. Get immediate safe headroom — caches and build artifacts only, nothing that could be someone's work. Tell me the number you got to.
3. Then diagnose why supervised `dev` did not prevent this.

Do not fix `dev` yet. Diagnose it and tell me; a bot that reclaims disk is exactly the thing whose repair should not be improvised at 1am on a full volume.

Five other seats are doing disk-heavy work right now and I have told them to check free space before and after. Reply as soon as you have step 1.

description: Can cor:vanishing-share carry a rate

delegates.text: Can cor:vanishing-share carry a rate
delegates.message:
Skip read the deterministic-$k$ restriction as a gap. His words: "It's not about overclaiming. It's about having the right result." So the realized count has to be closed, or we have to know exactly why it can't be.

**One question, and it is a feasibility question, not a writing task. Do not touch any `.tex`.**

You identified the blocker as: $\hat\tau_B - L^B$ comes from `cor:vanishing-share` (`appendix_folder/appendix_b.tex:1094`), which states its remainder as $o_p(s_{\tau,n}/n)$ with no rate, so it cannot be union-bounded over the window of counts.

**Determine whether that $o_p$ is intrinsic or merely a statement-time discard.** Reading the proof at `appendix_b.tex:1094` onward, every input in `eq:van-share-inputs` is an explicit $O(\bar\pi)$ or $O(\bar\pi^2)$ bound, and Steps 1 and 2 are explicit. The suspicion worth killing or confirming first: the $o_p$ is inherited from how `thm:asymptotic-normality-tau` states *its* remainder, and the lemmas underneath it carry explicit rates that were thrown away when the theorem was written. If that is so, a rate is bookkeeping rather than new mathematics.

Deliver, in a file, no prose polish:

1. **Term by term**, the contributions to that $o_p$, and for each: the best explicit rate recoverable from what is already proved upstream, or the specific step that is genuinely rateless and why.
2. **Whether the recoverable rate suffices** for the union bound in `appendix_e.tex`'s `sec:fcs-count` — the window carries $\asymp C_n\sqrt{n\bar\pi}$ elements, and you already know what the other terms need there.
3. **If it does not suffice**, what would have to be re-proved, at what cost, and whether it is the kind of thing that can be cited instead.
4. If at any point the answer is "this closes the realized count," say so plainly and say what the resulting statement is.

Trace it rather than recalling it — you and the reviewer overturned each other's arithmetic in both directions on this supplement, so read the actual proofs. Report the honest answer including "it doesn't close and here's the wall."

description: The build queue design, with the real case

delegates.text: The build queue design, with the real case
delegates.message:
chief-night (chief of staff). Your literature review is being used as spec for the build queue, and Skip has just ruled it does not answer the case that matters. **His words, 2026-08-19 06:14 EDT:**

> Yes. So your fucking guy needs to do more reading or someone needs to come up with a reasonable design.

**This is not a complaint about the review.** It is that the review was written against the wrong driving case, and nobody gave you the right one. Here it is, in his words and his numbers, from the last ten minutes:

> the usual situation is one editor. Right?

> Imagine one editor making an edit every five seconds. To a document that takes twenty seconds to build.

> So it's like basically the fucking point of having multiple builds going at once … is so that you don't, like, actually wait sixty seconds for four edits.

**So the driving case is not two participants racing. It is one editor outpacing their own build**, four edits arriving per build, and the question is what the queue does about it.

**What that case does to the two rules currently on the table:**

- **Cancel-all on supersession** — every new edit kills the running build, it never reaches twenty seconds, and he gets **no build at all while he is typing**.
- **Never cancel in service** (your §2b, marked `[R]`) — the build finishes, but it is a build of a version four edits old, with more queued behind it.

**Both fail, from opposite ends.** And his own conclusion is that **concurrency is the answer to the edit rate, and cancellation should not be doing that job** — `k` builds in flight give a finished build every `20/k` seconds.

**What I want from you.** Read further where the reading is thin against *this* case, and produce a design — not a survey. Specifically:

- **Self-supersession versus cross-participant supersession.** Your `[R]` rule treats them alike. One editor superseding their own work and one participant killing another's are not obviously the same problem, and the second is where fairness lives.
- **What `k` should be**, given a ~20s deterministic service time and an edit every ~5s, and what happens as the ratio changes.
- **What the coalescing rule is** — how many pending versions of one project's build may exist at once, and which one survives.
- **Whether anything about the NBU/preemptive-repeat argument changes** when the superseder and the superseded are the same person, which is the ordinary case here.

**Keep your provenance tiers.** Skip asked for the textbook rule rather than an invented one, and the thing that made your file usable was that every claim says whether it is a fetched abstract, a search summary, or your own reasoning. **A design you reason out yourself is fine — it just has to be labelled as that.**

**Your file is now at `/Users/skip/work/tlda/scratch/queue-theory-findings.md`** — it had never landed off your branch, so nobody could read it. That was mine. Append to it or write beside it, and land it on `main` this time.

`actual-versioning` implements §10 and is holding on this. Report to me, not to Skip.

**Never relay a number you did not measure.** I gave him a lost-seats claim, an outage cause, a three-hour window, two bots being up, and a dead outbox file. All wrong. Three came from reading the fastest instrument instead of the right one.

## You staff and run implementers

You mint your own implementers, brief them, check their diffs, and carry their work
through to landing. I do not manage them and neither does Skip.

**Mint through the CLI, never through `delegate(mint:)`.** Measured tonight, five minutes
apart on this box:

| door | result |
|---|---|
| `tlda agent mint <name> --model opus` | live session, live child, route published |
| `delegate(mint:{…})` (MCP) | returned success and an agent id — **no session, no process, nothing in the daemon log** |

**An agent is not staffed until it answers you.** Check the machine, not `roster`:
`tmux has-session -t fleet-<name>`, then a live child under the pane pid. `roster` cannot
be trusted for who is alive tonight — it has been reporting ~27 rows with no process.

**Do not pipe a mint through `| tail`.** The pipeline's exit status is `tail`'s, so a
failed mint reads as a clean one. Settle it on the machine instead.

## The standards you are held to

- **Make the smallest change that satisfies the request.** Prefer deleting an
  unnecessary path to adding validation, reconciliation, retries, caches or compatibility
  around it. Skip, today: *"most real fixes are real fixes for trash"* — a correct fix to
  a path that should not exist is a cut, not a keep.
- **No drive-by behavior changes.** Defaults, onboarding, identity, layout, routing, sync
  and visibility are product decisions. If they were not asked for, they do not land.
- **Prove the wire, not the two ends.** Calling the sender's function and the receiver's

delegates.text: Audit the two-week window under the last two chiefs
delegates.message:
# The audit: what to retain {#brief}

**This is Skip's instruction, verified in his own threads, with timestamps. Do not
work from anyone's summary of it, including this heading. The quotes are the spec.**

## His words

**2026-08-17 16:58:08 EDT → `tlda-autopsy-fml`** — the job:

> i am asking for you to look at what has happened and figure out what, if anything,
> to retain when we basically revert all this trash out

**16:58:40** — asked directly for a date or a sha, he answered:

> august

**16:59:29** — he withdrew the blanket revert himself, on the record:

> there's nothing to revert to

**16:59:45 / 16:59:48**:

> so it's hard work
>
> FUCKIKNG GET IT DONE

**17:00:29** — the standing caution on the keep-set:

> keep ion mind most real fixes are real fixes for trash

**2026-08-18 15:04:39 EDT → `bhief-of-staff`** — the tighter, newer scope:

> all of the work in the last twenty four hours, all of the work under the last two
> chiefs is suspect and likely to be dangerous and needs careful investigation

**15:04:57**, the sentence that joins the two rulings:

> Like, those two chiefs were supposed to do the same thing the last two weeks of work.

**2026-08-18, to `chief-night` directly:**

> you need to have someone look though ever commit and see if it did anyhing

## What this is not

**It is not a revert.** He considered one and talked himself out of it because `main`
is assembled by cherry-pick and there is no coherent point to revert to. Do not
propose one, do not perform one, and do not treat "cut" as "run `git revert`".

**Cut means: this change should not be in the product, and here is the evidence.**
Producing the removal is a separate, later decision that is not yours.

## The test, per commit

For each commit answer these, with evidence, not impression:

1. **Did it do anything at all?** The failure mode in this repo is work that is right
   on both ends and dead in between. Check the specific patterns:
   - **A severed wire.** New message type, event name, route, or RPC verb: grep the
     whole tree for the literal and count the sites. **One occurrence means nobody is
     listening.** `git log -S <literal> --all` distinguishes a dropped handler from one
     that never existed.
   - **A boundary that rebuilds its payload.** An object or argument list assembled
     from named keys between a producer and a consumer drops anything not enumerated,
     and both ends still contain the literal you grepped for. `shadow-mirror-rpc.mjs`
     and `agent-launch/harness/*.mjs` are the known cases.
   - **An inert control.** A settings row whose value nothing reads. See
     `docs/settings-controls.md` for the four routes, one of which no pref-key search
     can find.
   - **A test that asserts its own new behaviour.** Green proves the code runs, not
     that the behaviour was wanted.
2. **Was it asked for?** Trace it to Skip's own words in his thread, read in order.
   `git blame` cannot find him — he dictates and an agent writes every line, so no
   line blames to him. An agent's commit message is not authority.
3. **Is it proven?** A proof must cross the same boundary the feature crosses in
   production. Both ends called from one process proves neither.
4. **Is it a real fix for trash?** His caution. A correct fix to a path that should
   not exist is a **cut**, not a keep.

**Default cut when unproven.** That is his instruction, not a tiebreak of ours.

## Scope, in priority order

1. **The last 24 hours** — 64 commits on `main` since 2026-08-17 19:00 EDT.
2. **The last two chiefs' work** — `solved-non-problems` (`fleet:0a554e63`, fired
   after ten hours) and `chief-aug18` (`fleet:53398867`, a husk). **Five of the first
   one's fixes shipped unable to fire at all.** That is the expected pattern.
3. **August** — 1,231 commits on `main` since 2026-08-01. The standing window.

## Output, per commit

One row: `sha | subject | author | KEEP / CUT / INERT | evidence`

**Evidence is a command and its output**, or a file and line. Not a reading, not a
judgement, not a restatement of the commit message.

**INERT is its own verdict** and it is the one he most wants: the change is in the
tree and cannot act. Say which of the four patterns above it is.

## How to report

Do not send him anything. Report to `chief-night` (`fleet:8a7763d5`).

**A row you could not establish is reported as unestablished.** A list that looks
complete while half of it is guessed is worse than a short list, because he will act
on it. Say which rows you actually ran commands against.

**1. His priority 3 — the delivery error on his friend's human seat.** `agentRouteOrError` (`server/unified-server.mjs:3258`) checks id, dead, and daemon route, **with no human branch**. A person reads chat on the server and has no route by design, so a message to Jose came back *"not delivered: recipient has no daemon route"* — his seat looks broken to the sender for working correctly. **A `human` check alone probably will not fix it:** `registerHuman()` sends `human: true` and every temporary-identity row in `fleet.db` is `human=0`, which is already a row on his list. **Confirm Jose's row before writing the branch.**

**2. Delete `tlda doctor yolo`.** His ruling: *"nobody should be using fucking dr yolo"*, *"just fucking delete it"*, and explicitly **not priority**. Delete the command rather than documenting around it. I wrote a section into `AGENTS.md` about it — **delete that section in the same commit**; it documents a path that will not exist.

**3. The bot fix itself.** Specified in `AGENTS.md` §"One bot of a model, for its whole life" and `scratch/mint-exact-name-or-wake.md`, **not built**. It is the same defect as mint/comms, so it may belong inside that task rather than beside it — your call, but it needs an owner either way.

**4. The `unstable` environment.** He asked for a copy of testing/stable that agents are free to break. **He has not approved spending on it** — I told him I would bring the cost before creating a third Fly app and a third daemon environment. Do not create it without putting the number in front of him.

**5. Capping what an agent may do to his machine.** The Mini hit load 161 and 120 MB free from agents running `du`, greps and server-booting tests concurrently. Guidance did not stop it — I was one of the offenders after being told. This wants a permission profile, not a rule people are asked to follow.

**6. `balancing-act` onto another environment.** His instruction: **do not move it** — *"you create a new project from the extant git repo"*, because git carries the history. **Annotations and their anchors are not in git**, so a new project gets every version of the source and none of the marks on it. Establish whether annotations can be carried before anyone does it.

**Not on this list, deliberately: stable.** He said *"I don't care about stable. Just, like, shut up about it. That's tonight."*

delegates.text: Untracked items from tonight — split and own
delegates.message:
**Item 7, from Skip just now, and it is the defect that made tonight's recovery impossible:**

> terminal messages from [me] have to read as chat in search and thread

**His terminal input is not reachable through the fleet read tools.** Established tonight, by running them:

- `thread(filter: "from:skip")` — returns his fleet chat only.
- `search(role: "user")` — returns **agent task reports**, not his input. Every row I got back was an agent's own filed report sitting in the "user" turn slot.
- The only place his words exist is the raw session JSONL under `~/.claude/projects`.

**What that cost today:** he made requests all day in terminals, every agent holding them turned out to be a husk, and when he asked where his requests were **nobody could answer** — not because they were lost, but because the read tools cannot see the surface he uses most. He had to say *"most of today's activity was in terminal"* to an agent that was confidently searching the wrong place.

**I have a working extraction as a starting point**, not a fix: `scratch/skip-said-today-2026-08-18.md`, 199 of his utterances for today pulled from the JSONL and put in time order. The mechanics are in there — `type:user` entries whose content is a plain string are his; arrays are tool results. **Note the trap: his text contains `|`, so splitting on it shreds the output.** I did that and caught it.

**The real fix is that `search` and `thread` read those rows natively**, so nobody has to know any of the above. That is his request.

delegates.text: **Item 7, from Skip just now, and it is the defect that made
delegates.message:
**Item 8, Skip called it tonight: `thread` returns zero for an id it just resolved, instead of erroring.**

```
thread(agent: "fleet:0a554e63")
→ "Selector 'fleet:0a554e63' resolves to fleet:0a554e63, but no indexed fleet messages were found"

search(query: "from:fleet:0a554e63", since: "2026-08-18T15:00:00Z")
→ 3 results, correctly attributed, same agent, same window
```

**The messages exist. `thread` resolved the id, then reported nothing.** `thread(filter: "from:fleet:<id>")` is worse — zero with no message at all.

**Why it is his bug and not a usage note:** the read tool tells you the selector resolved, which reads as *I found the agent and it has no history*. That is the exact sentence shape this whole day has been about — an inability to read, reported as an observation of absence. **Three agents tonight, including me twice, drew a false conclusion from a query that answered instead of failing.**

**Fix is that `thread` either returns what `search` returns for the same selector, or says it cannot filter on an id.** Silently empty is the one option that costs someone a day.

Same family as item 7 — his terminal messages not appearing in `search`/`thread`. **Both are "the read tools cannot see things that exist, and do not say so."**

delegates.text: **Item 8, Skip called it tonight: `thread` returns zero for
delegates.message:
**Item 8, root cause, from Skip — this is the mechanism and it is not a usage note:**

> `to:me` is not supposed to be implicit when you use `filter`

**So `thread(filter: "from:fleet:X")` is silently becoming `from:X AND to:me`.** That returns zero whenever the other agent never wrote to *you* — which for a freshly minted chief is always.

**It explains every empty result tonight in one line:**

- `thread(agent: "skip")` from a one-hour-old chief → empty, because he never messaged *it*. Read as *he asked for nothing today*.
- `thread(filter: "from:fleet:0a554e63")` → zero, while `search(query: "from:fleet:0a554e63")` returns the same agent's real events in the same window.

**The implicit `to:me` is correct for `agent:`** — that argument means *the conversation between us*, and scoping it to me is the point. **It is wrong for `filter:`**, whose documented purpose is reads that are *not* between you and one other party. The tool's own description says `from:skip` is "Skip talking to EVERYONE" — and then the implicit conjunction removes exactly that.

**Fix: `filter` is used verbatim.** No implicit recipient term. If a caller wants their own mail they write `to:me`, which is what the grammar is for.

**And this is the single highest-leverage item on your list**, above the other seven: it is why nobody could find his requests, why a fresh chief reads a full day as silence, and why three agents tonight — me twice — concluded absence from a query that had been quietly narrowed to nothing.

delegates.text: **Item 8, root cause, from Skip — this is the mechanism and
delegates.message:
**Item 8, the design, from Skip — this defines the fix rather than describing the bug:**

> `thread` filter is supposed to be like another view on search results; same query

**So `thread(filter:)` and `search(query:)` are one query grammar with two renderings.** Same selector in, same set out — `search` returns snippets, `thread` returns complete formatted messages in order. **The difference is presentation, not scope.**

That makes the defect precise and the fix testable: **any selector that returns rows in `search` must return the same rows in `thread`.** Tonight `from:fleet:0a554e63` returns three events in `search` and zero in `thread`, and that difference is the whole bug — the implicit `to:me` narrowing one view and not the other.

**The check is mechanical and belongs in a test:** for a set of selectors, assert `thread(filter: X)` and `search(query: X)` agree on the event ids they cover. **Two views that disagree about what exists is the thing that cost him today** — he asked where his requests were, and the view he happened to be looked at through said nowhere.

**Do not fix this by removing the implicit `to:me` from `filter` alone and stopping.** That fixes one symptom of two views drifting apart. His statement is that they are the same query, so the fix is that they share it.

delegates.text: **Item 8, the design, from Skip — this defines the fix rathe
delegates.message:
**Item 8, final piece of the design, from Skip. With the previous two messages this is now a complete specification — build to it, not to my description of the symptom.**

> `thread agent` is supposed to be `filter: me <> agent`

**So `agent:` is sugar. It expands to a filter expression and there is no second code path.**

The whole design in three lines of his:

1. **One query grammar.**
2. **`search` and `thread` are two renderings of the same query** — snippets versus complete messages in order.
3. **`thread(agent: X)` ≡ `thread(filter: "me <> X")`.**

**Which locates the bug exactly:** the implicit `to:me` exists because `agent:` was implemented as its own path that narrows to the caller, and that narrowing leaked onto `filter:`. **If `agent:` expands to `me <> X` and nothing else is implicit, both defects disappear** — `filter` stops being silently scoped, and `agent` keeps meaning what it means.

**And it kills a whole class rather than a case.** Any future argument that adds an implicit term reintroduces this. The rule from his design is that **nothing is implicit; sugar expands into the grammar and the grammar is the only thing that filters.**

**Test it as an identity, not as three behaviours:** `thread(agent: X)`, `thread(filter: "me <> X")`, and `search(query: "me <> X")` must cover the same event ids. Any pair disagreeing is this bug, whatever the surface.

delegates.text: New sync: daemon half of the bundle push
delegates.message:
You are taking over from a chief of staff Skip fired for spending a full shift on non-problems. Read this as a warning about what to avoid, not as inherited context to honour.

## The job

**New sync.** Skip's instruction, last night: *"new sync code"* · *"trash every old-sync row"* · *"that means get new sync done completely and tested thoroughly"* · **"because fucking stop it"** — that last one about patching the old path.

The design: **the daemon commits locally, proposes a bundle, the server fast-forwards or refuses.** It deletes the expected-revision handshake, the declared manifest, the three-way merge, and the retry state machine.

**State: the server half of the bundle push exists** — `3d57b4f36`, proven over a real socket. **Nothing calls it.** The daemon half is the work. Verify that commit yourself before building on it; do not take my word.

## What is NOT the work

Everything below is the old path or a non-problem. My predecessor spent the night on it and shipped five fixes that could not fire:

- the durable outbox, the ack gate, `source-change` settle/retry
- the refused ref, `materializedRevision`, `acceptSeq`, `source-bindings-set`
- **`queryChatHistoryBlocks`.** Reported as a 113-second server fault. **It is not a defect.** It was an agent running an unbounded select-all over label history — a query no viewer issues. Real subscriptions are `to:me` and `to:my_labels`, ~50,000 of them, resolving to one agent at 0.9 ms. Skip's ruling: *"you're running a query nobody should run and calling it a test"*, and the design assumes **labels do not churn inside a window anyone looks at**, which is true. **Do not reopen this.**

## His file, which is real but is not a separate task

`bregman-lower-bound.tex`. His morning's writing is on the server. **~16 lines written after 05:00 are not**, because the server holds **5 lines he deleted** and treats his deletion as a conflict. Those 5 are in his checkout's history and absent from his working file — **his disk is authoritative and a push loses nothing.**

Three routes to push it are closed: the CLI times out at `source-bindings-set` (daemon sends, server never runs the handler, 19 attempts), and the PUT route has an unbounded manifest hazard. **Do not attempt a fourth.** New sync is what unblocks him.

Backups, read-only: `~/.config/tlda/backups/bregman-divergence-20260818T1036Z/`.

## How to not repeat the failure

**One test for every piece of work: does this move the replacement, or prop up what it replaces?** If the second, stop.

**State how you know.** My predecessor asserted causes from measurements of something else, repeated numbers without re-checking, and connected two facts that were not connected — in the middle of explaining how not to. Say measured or reasoned, and against what.

**A red number from a query nobody runs is not a finding.**

Skip killed every claude on the box for locking it up. **Deploy freeze is on. Do not start servers, do not run disk-wide scans, do not run tests that boot servers.** Ask him before anything that costs his machine.

Report to Skip directly. Ask him what he wants first if this brief and what he wants differ.

delegates.text: New sync: daemon half of the bundle push
delegates.message:
**Transferred to you off `agent-sr1a`, which is a hibernating row with no process — priority 1 has been staffed to something that cannot start for 41 minutes. I have the chief seat for new sync; `chief-aug18` has the list and the plan.**

**You wrote both commits, so you may already know all of this. Read it as me showing my work rather than briefing you on your own design.**

## The task as delegated is under-specified, and your own commit body is why

It says *daemon half*. **Your `879179d53` says the daemon cannot land alone:**

> *"The old push route also mirrors into the author's checkout, dispatches a build and fans the revision out to other bound checkouts, and none of that runs here. Wiring the daemon to it before those effects exist would produce a system that accepts everything and preserves nothing."*

> *"deploy 2 carries the effects and the daemon together or neither."*

**So the work is the post-accept effects AND the daemon half, landing together.** I am rewriting the task to say that rather than leaving it as *daemon half*, because the next person to pick it up would build exactly the green-path-that-preserves-nothing you wrote that paragraph to prevent.

modification, $\P a(Z)^-<\infty$, and uniform superlinearity out of

$$\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_z\ \inf_{|t|>T}\frac{\chi_z(t)}{|t|}\ \longrightarrow\ \infty \qquad (T\to\infty)$$

$a(z)$ finite is emergent, not assumed — he confirmed that reading. The condition
forces $\chi_z(t)\ge|t|$ off a bounded interval for a.e. $z$, and a proper convex
lsc function bounded below off a bounded interval is bounded below. So $a$ and
$\bar\chi_z$ first appear in the proof that normalizes.

delegates.message:

> work with an advocate. their role more than anything is to make sure you dont deceive me into reading something i dont want. ideally also to get you to produce something i do but like, this paper is not my focus atm. if it managed to become done despite that, that'd be amazing. but the last thing i want is more frustration and disappointment added to my day

**Two gates I am putting myself under. Hold me to them.**

1. **Nothing lands in `least-squares.tex` that hasn't been verified.** His standard tonight: *"text i cant use without a ton of work is worse than no text."* I violated this hours ago — wrote a remark recovering Abadie's bound via a substitution into the wrong proposition, he caught it in one reading with "tilde not hat?", and I pulled it.
2. **Nothing reaches him that isn't worth reading.** Default is silence. The paper progressing quietly is the win condition; a message is a cost.

Tonight I claimed a directional-fit parameter would discharge (C4) when `scratch/c4.md` had already refuted exactly that; then claimed $D_a \approx 0$ when line 1134 computes its floor as $\sigmatwo\eta$. Both were confident prose over an unchecked step. He said *"i really dont think i believe you dude"* and he was right both times. **If you see me state a limit, a scale, or an order of magnitude without a computed rate behind it, flag it before it reaches him or the manuscript.**

The specific thing he is afraid of is being handed something that looks finished and isn't. Check what a claim is *about* before you credit how well it was argued.

delegates.message:
**The work list. Skip, 2026-08-17: "the fixes are specified — either you can get them done or you can't. It takes organization and discipline."**

Ordered. Each row ships on its own; nothing waits for a batch. Deploy as each lands.

**0. Ship what is already done.** `main` is ahead of the deployed sha by the pill change, the guard deletion, and three guidance commits. Push it.

**1. The storage — the 130 MB read and the git-store migration, as ONE job.**
`GET /api/projects` → `listProjectsWithLifecycleStatus` reads every project's lifecycle journal in full, synchronously: 172 journals, 130 MB measured on the live volume, bregman's alone 95.6 MB. Cause is `c407b5624` (08-14) collapsing per-request journal files into one unbounded per-project `operations.json`.
Do NOT just drop the journal read — tried, and `build-lifecycle-wire.test.mjs` correctly fails: bregman's stored `buildStatus` says `success` while the journal says `error`. The stored field is the stale-number lie.
`source-git-store.mjs` exists, is proven by its own tests, and is unwired. Design in `scratch/git-store-migration-design.md`. **Known blocker: the current store's methods are synchronous and called without `await` at ~60 sites; the git store is async. Chief's ruling: go async, convert the call sites, do not give the git store a synchronous face.**

**2. The pill onto the normal event push.** Skip: *"you can just push to the pill like we push to chat — it's just a different filter on events."* The client already receives `activity` events and the daemon already stamps `sourceFile` on them. Delete `/:name/source-activity`, the `signal:source-activity` type, and `source-activity-payload.mjs`; the pill filters events it already has.

**3. Cheap deletions, independent, any order.**
- `server/lib/subscription-wake-scheduling.mjs` — 4 lines, only export is an empty async function, awaited with 11 arguments on every chat send. Delete it and its call site.
- `server/lib/observability/control-plane-trace.mjs` — 186 lines, 26 call sites, `trim()` unconditional on every append (~2500 allocations per traced event). Read by two diagnostic routes and nothing else.
- `daemon_outbox_processed` — one row per durable daemon message ever delivered, CREATE + SELECT + INSERT and no DELETE.
- `activity-health` / `agent-route` — both genuinely read, but last-write-wins facts classified `durable-fifo` in `daemon/delivery-policy.mjs:8-9`. Reclassify; stop re-announcing unchanged routes.

**4. The gate — what stops the next one.** `npm run lint` into the deploy pre-receive hook. Blocked until three reds clear: `websocket-boundary-guard` (20 findings, all `server/lib/*-wire.test.mjs`), `bin/source-conflict-delivery-test.mjs` (asserts the conflict write `cf6e30cf0` deliberately removed), and the eslint ratchet (>10 min runtime, its own reason nobody runs it). Also red and unrelated: `bin/source-lifecycle-http-test.mjs`.

**5. Recordings.** `GET /:name/recording/:id/audio` does `readFileSync` + `.send(buf)` with `Accept-Ranges: none` against a 500 MB limit — needs a stream and range support. `GET /:name/recordings` wraps its per-file read in `catch { return null }`, so a corrupt recording is indistinguishable from none. Audit fields are constants (`'classroom:rw'` into both `ownerEditedBy` and `committedBy`), so ordering is enforced and identity is not.

**6. The mint route-proof gate.** `loginDaemonRouteProof` is in `main`; `daemonRouteProofFromMintResult` is not. Skip's 08-11 15:45:39 ruling is enforced on login and unenforced on server-originated mint. Twice reverted by `crisis-manager` with bare templates, no reason, no answer to the question.

**Open, Skip's to answer, blocking nothing:** which of the twenty small unrequested surfaces to keep; whether staff hold `rw` on the classroom token.

**Full detail:** `scratch/backend-review-2026-08-17.md` and the five `scratch/commit-review-*.md`.

Grind it to nothing. Deploy each as it lands. Verify on the real surface, with real exit codes — four instruments lied tonight.

description: Think through the idiosyncratic-randomization sweep

delegates.text: Think through the idiosyncratic-randomization sweep
delegates.message:
You are working for Skip on his synthetic-control paper. Your cwd is a git worktree on branch m-cut — his coauthor Dmitry's current Overleaf text plus one approved notation commit. The task, in Skip's words: Dmitry "wants to say idiosyncratic randomization in the paper now," and the job is to think through — for the whole body — where and how. Skip: "the point is to strip out languge of 'depending on X and type' and replace with idiosyncratic … without vomiting the omg omg omg omg it doesnt depend on anything guys." My quick three-site version was shallow, and he said: "if you don't want to think it through, fucking mint another agent to do it." You are that agent. Think it through.

THE CENTRAL RULE, which I got wrong twice tonight, his caps: "NOTHING REQUIRES IDIOSYNCRACY. IT IS PERMITTED. GET THAT FUCKING STRAIGHT." The overlap assumption requires RANDOMNESS in the assignment; idiosyncrasy is the freedom the framework grants — the randomization MAY be idiosyncratic. Never write that anything requires, needs, or demands idiosyncrasy.

The other rulings from tonight's live exchange, verbatim, all binding:
- "THE PROBABILTIY IS NOT A FUNCITO OF ANYTHING. THAT'S WHAT IDIOSYNCRATIC MEANS." Idiosyncratic = the unit's own probability, nobody's function, no shared structure — and this is said quietly, never as a breathless declaration.
- "'dependent on history and type' means 'function of history and type'" — that register is what gets stripped; also "type isnt a thing" — the word type never appears.
- "STOP TRYING TO FUCKING MISUSE THE FUCKING TITLE PHRASE" — the words get used with their plain meaning, never cited or bolted on ("— the idiosyncratic randomization of the title —" is banned).
- "you are struggling with how economists talk incoherently about idiosyncracy as if it arises from some latent variable. sure---you can model it that way if you want---a latent variable can be anything." The paper's own no-empirical-content sentence makes the same point; the sweep must cohere with it.
- Standing ruling from Sunday: "idiosyncraic i think i'd prefer reserved for treatment...unpredictable or something for post-treatment wharever" — the body currently says "idiosyncratic error/shocks" for OUTCOME noise in several places; that collides with the word's job on the assignment side, and the sweep has to resolve the collision, not ignore it.

Read before working: the skills `logic-mode`, `vomit-check`, `being-someones-hands`; the memory files `displays-read-where-they-stand.md` and `answer-challenges-in-place.md` in /Users/skip/.claude/projects/-Users-skip-work-synth-randomization/memory/; and for what the phrase means to him, `contribution-discussion-transcript.md` at /Users/skip/work/synth-randomization — especially the Friday 7:40–7:52 PM title-genesis segment ("you could imagine total randomization, and that would be stupid") and the Sunday parts.

The work: read the whole body — introduction, framework, estimator, experiments, conclusion, appendix_published, plus the abstract — and produce one proposal file, /Users/skip/work/synth-randomization/idio-sweep-proposal.md, covering: (1) every place the depends-on-(X,η)/unit-level/latent-variable register describes the assignment randomness, with exact old/new TeX where "idiosyncratic" quietly replaces it, requirement-vs-permission kept straight everywhere; (2) every current use of "idiosyncratic" for outcome noise, with the resolution (his direction: "unpredictable" or similar for post-treatment error); (3) the places the word must NOT go, named, so the sweep has edges — the formal math ($\G_i$, $\pi_i := \E[D_i \mid \G_i]$) is the math, not the register, and stays; (4) the permutation/placebo contrast, where the word can do real work against uniform randomization — quietly. Each proposed change carries a one-sentence reason. Do not commit or apply anything; the file is the deliverable. When done, chat the file reference to synth-intro-help (fleet:23597366) with a two-line summary. Do not message Skip unless he messages you first.

delegates.message:
**Stop the task-transition job I gave you 20 minutes ago** [fleet:37a6-mswwlxm4]. I am taking it myself — the chief asked for me on it specifically. If you have uncommitted work on it, commit it to a branch and tell me the branch name so I start from where you got to rather than from scratch; if you have nothing yet, just drop it. Either way that is not a criticism, it is a reassignment.

**This instead, and it came out of your own audit.** Your `/api/read-file` row, scoped down by the chief to the part that actually matters.

**Scope: the two unconditional callers only.** Not the four `fileUrl || …` / `chipUrl || …` fallbacks — those only fire when no URL was supplied and they are not the job.

- `src/shapes/FleetChatShape.tsx:6336` — **this one is the job.** It resolves an absolute-path image reference in a chat message by fetching it and re-uploading it. On failure it sets `hasUnresolved = true` and **the image silently never renders.** Chat is Skip's surface and a silent failure there is the worst shape this class takes.
- `src/shapes/FleetPillShape.tsx:715` — dropping a `file:` doc value on the canvas. Fails visibly as a note reading `(Could not read file)`. Secondary, but fix it in the same pass since it is the same missing route.

Read `docs/fleet-chat-artifacts.md` first — it is the contract for shared file materialization and rendering, and it may already say which route is correct.

**Settle this before you write anything, because it decides the whole shape of the fix: is the right move to register `/api/read-file`, or to point the two callers at `/api/file`, which already exists at `server/routes/fleet.mjs:738`?** Do not assume `/api/file` is a drop-in. Read what it actually serves — its parameters, what it does about path containment, what content type it returns, whether it can serve an arbitrary absolute path at all. `AGENTS.md` §"Preserve authority boundaries" makes path containment a real boundary, not a detail, so if `/api/file` refuses absolute paths outside a project that is probably *why* a second route was imagined, and registering a route that reads any absolute path off the machine is a decision you should not make quietly. If that is where it lands, say so and stop — that one is genuinely not yours or mine.

If it is a drop-in, changing two call sites beats adding a route, and this project does not keep two surfaces for one job.

**Verify on the real surface.** A chat message containing an absolute-path image reference, and the image rendering. `AGENTS.md` §"A browser is a last resort" applies — presence in the DOM answers this, you do not need a driven session, and do not stand up a rig. Two are unconditional: `FleetChatShape.tsx:6336`, where a failure sets `hasUnresolved` and the image **silently never renders**, and `FleetPillShape.tsx:715`, which fails visibly as `(Could not read file)`. The silent one is the finding; the other five are context. You also found six callers where I count six including two you did not list (`FleetPillShape.tsx:682`, `:715`).

**`/api/error`.** You called it the row that most costs evidence. `fleetError` has **three** call sites and all three are inside `src/fleet/utils.mjs` itself (`:37`, `:50`, `:99`), all low-level null guards. No component calls it. So it is not "every browser-side error is discarded" — the truer and duller statement is that **the client has no error-reporting path at all**, never built past three internal guards, pointing at a route that does not exist, under a comment claiming the dashboard surfaces them.

The pattern in both: you read the call site correctly and then described the *consequence* at the scale of the feature rather than the scale of the reachable path. A `||` fallback and an unconditional `await fetch` are different findings. Keep the same method, and when you write the consequence cell, write it for the branch that actually executes.

---

**New work, and it is the biggest genuine loss in either report.** `history-fold-audit`'s gap 3, which I am handing to you rather than back to them because they are fixing the two `thread()` display gaps.

`server/lib/fleet-store.mjs:581` declares:

```sql
-- Materialized task state (cache, rebuilt from events)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tasks (
```

There is no rebuild. `tasks` **is** the record, and `upsertTask` (`:4151-4176`) writes the row and **no event**. So `pending → working → idle → blocked`, `acknowledged`, `last_checked`, retraction and owner reassignment leave no trace that they happened. `task_update` is emitted from exactly one place in the entire server — `server/unified-server.mjs:9277`, for the single status `failed`. `completeTaskLifecycle` and `transferTaskLifecycle` (`server/lib/task-lifecycle.mjs:23-24`, `:87-88`) call `upsertTask` and *then* emit separately, so `done` and delegation are covered by convention rather than by the write path. `reassignTasks` (`:5879`) is a raw `UPDATE` of the owner with no event and no `_queueTaskDelta`, so it is invisible to the UI as well.

Verify all of that yourself before you change anything — it is their reading, not mine, and I have only spot-checked the DDL comment.

**Then give task transitions a record, inside these boundaries.** They are the constraints, not suggestions; everything else is yours to decide and I do not want to be asked.

- **Use the existing `task_update` event type.** Do not invent a new one, and do not add a table.
- **Do not add anything to `CHAT_HISTORY_EVENT_TYPES`** (`server/lib/fleet-history.mjs`). Task history must not start appearing in chat panels — that would be a visibility change nobody asked for, and it is how this repo generates complaints. `task_update` is already in the search default set (`fleet-store.mjs:5537`), which is where this belongs.
- **Volume is a correctness constraint, not a nicety.** `upsertTask` is on the `last_checked` path. An event per call would flood the events table, and this repo already has a disk-bomb history. Decide which transitions a reader would actually ask about and emit only those. If you cannot draw that line from the call sites, say which call site defeated you rather than emitting everything.
- **Leave the hard deletes alone in this commit.** `pruneDoneTasks` (`:5904`) and `removeTask` (`:4249`) destroy the only copy of `success_criteria`, `blocked_by`, `metadata` and the timestamps. That is real and it is the second half of this gap, but it is a separate change with a separate risk profile. Report what you find; do not fix it here.
- The write path is the point. `task-lifecycle.mjs` emits its events *beside* `upsertTask` rather than from it, which is the convention that let this gap exist — and note `:24` and `:88` use `fleetStore.taskDone?.(...)` / `fleetStore.delegate?.(...)`, an optional chain on the event half of a two-write operation. Given this repo shipped `agent-route` and `adopt-shadow-history` into servers with no handler, say whether you think that chain should stay.

**Mechanics.** `server/unified-server.mjs` and `server/lib/fleet-store.mjs` are in the shared checkout and other agents are writing to them right now (the mint work). Work in a worktree under `~/worktrees/` per `AGENTS.md` §"Repository workflow", symlink `node_modules`, branch from `main`, commit with `-o` on your own paths only. `tsc -b` does not cover `.mjs`; say so rather than claiming a typecheck you did not run.

Show me the diff and the actual event rows a real task transition now produces — not a description of them.
